answer: One practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable history rather than to a free username. Think of a garden where every plot must be tended over time: a newcomer cannot plant a thousand identical identities overnight. An umber-stained record of completed work, peer attestations and slashed deposits accumulates slowly, so each extra identity costs real effort. A relic of past behaviour, signed receipts that cannot be forged or transferred, lets others weight new claims by proven history, making mass fakes expensive and easy to spot.
